blocks.text: The oxides of nitrogen are NO, N2O, NO2, N2O4 and N2O5, in which the oxidation states of nitrogen range from +1 to +5. N2O4 and N2O5 decay quickly to other oxides. NO and NO2 are collectively called NOx. Their structures, properties and uses are given in Table 12.2.

Middle left: the chain of smog reactions from nitrogen and oxygen to ozone and to peroxyacyl nitrate. Middle right: a honeycomb converter with exhaust gases entering and clean gases leaving, and its three redox equations. Bottom: nitrification and denitrification with their equations and conditions.

blocks.long_description: Nitrogen forms oxides from the sweet laughing gas N2O through the paramagnetic NO to the red-brown NO2 that dimerises to colourless N2O4 on cooling. Lightning and soil bacteria make nitrogen oxides naturally, but most come from burning fossil fuels in engines and power stations. In sunlight nitrogen dioxide splits to give oxygen atoms that make ozone, ozone oxidises hydrocarbons to aldehydes, and these go through acyl and peroxyacyl radicals that combine with nitrogen dioxide to form the eye-stinging peroxyacyl nitrates of photochemical smog. A three-way catalytic converter uses platinum, palladium and rhodium on a honeycomb to reduce nitric oxide with carbon monoxide and to oxidise carbon monoxide and hydrocarbons. In soil, aerobic bacteria oxidise ammonium to nitrite and nitrate for plants, and anaerobic bacteria reduce nitrate back to nitrogen gas.

blocks.prompt: Draw the structures of N2O, NO and NO2 and briefly explain their bonding (Quick Check 12.2a).
blocks.explanation: N2O is linear, N=N=O (or N-N triple bond to O-), with nitrogen in +1. NO has an odd number of electrons: a double bond N=O with one unpaired electron on nitrogen, hence paramagnetic, and it dimerises weakly to N2O2. NO2 is bent, O-N=O with a delocalised bond and an unpaired electron on nitrogen (paramagnetic), which pairs up when two molecules join through N-N to give N2O4.

items: Oxides NO, N2O, NO2, N2O4, N2O5 (N +1 to +5); N2O4 and N2O5 decay; NOx = NO + NO2.
N2O (+1): sweet, anaesthetic, propellant. NO (+2): paramagnetic, messenger. NO2 (+4): red-brown, gives HNO3 + HNO2 with water, 2NO2 = N2O4 colourless; rocket propellant, Ostwald process.
